item.title: Integrating Leadership and Green Human Resource Management for Sustainable and Thriving Workplaces
item.content:encoded:
Azadeh Shafaei, Edith Cowan University

Mehran Nejati, Edith Cowan University

This special issue examines how leadership and green human resource management integrate to create sustainable and thriving workplaces. As organisations face environmental and social pressures, they must embed sustainability into HR systems while supporting employee wellbeing. The issue seeks research on how leadership approaches influence GHRM design, implementation, and effectiveness, and their impact on employee and organisational outcomes.

Beyond celebrating sustainability initiatives, the special issue encourages critical examination of their challenges and downsides. Green practices can intensify work demands, create role ambiguity, generate cynicism when perceived as inauthentic greenwashing, or trigger stress and fatigue. Balanced analysis of both benefits and unintended consequences is welcomed.

Contributions are invited exploring leadership-driven GHRM mechanisms, contextual factors determining effectiveness, and employee experiences including wellbeing, engagement, inclusion, and psychological safety, alongside critical perspectives on paradoxes and negative aspects of sustainability-focused workplace initiatives.

Appel publié par Employee Relations. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Leadership and Green Human Resource Management (GHRM)
  • Sustainable Leadership and Employee Outcomes
  • Authenticity, Greenwashing, and Employee Responses to Sustainability Initiatives
  • The Bright and Dark Sides of Green Human Resource Management
  • Multi-Level, Cross-Cultural, and Digital Perspectives on Sustainable Workplaces

Timeline

  • January 2, 2027: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • January 6, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Guardians of accountability: Accounting professionals' roles in fraud prevention and early internal detection
item.content:encoded:
Domenico Campa, International University of Monaco

Dan-Richard Knudsen, NHH Norwegian School of Economics

Aziza Laguecir, EDHEC Business School

Accounting scandals persist despite regulatory reforms and enhanced audit scrutiny, indicating that fraud prevention requires deeper understanding of professional, organisational, and institutional conditions. This special issue addresses an under-researched area: how fraudulent practices can be prevented rather than merely investigated after disclosure, with particular attention to the roles of auditors, certified fraud examiners, and internal accountants as whistle-blowers.

The issue examines how organisational structures, institutional cultures, regulatory environments, and ethical climates influence fraud detection and prevention. It also considers emerging technologies such as blockchain and AI, which create both new fraud risks and detection opportunities, while raising questions about data control and algorithmic bias.

The special issue invites theoretical and empirical contributions that examine fraud prevention holistically, moving beyond compliance-focused approaches to explore the social, institutional, and moral dimensions of integrity and ethical decision-making in accounting contexts.

Appel publié par Accounting Forum. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
